title: Rumor That Spreads Then Fades
statement:
On day 1, exactly one person learns a rumor. Someone who learns it on day d:

  • tells one new person per day, starting on day d + delay,
  • forgets it on day d + forget, and from that day on neither knows nor tells it. A person never tells anyone on the day they forget.

Return how many people know the rumor at the end of day n, modulo 1 000 000 007.

examples.why: New learners per day are 1, 1, 2, 3, 5. On day 5 everyone from days 1 and 2 has forgotten, leaving 2 + 3 + 5.
The first person tells one person on day 3 and forgets on day 4. That new person has not started telling yet, so only they remain.
New learners per day are 1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 2. Days 3 to 6 are still remembered: 1 + 1 + 1 + 2.

hints: Tracking people one by one explodes. Track how many people learn the rumor on each day instead.
Everyone who learned on day j tells someone on day d exactly when j + delay ≤ d < j + forget. So the new learners on day d are a sum over a range of earlier days.

Let fresh[d] be the number who learn on day d. fresh[d] = sum of fresh[j] for j from d − forget + 1 to d − delay. The answer sums fresh over the last forget days. Keep a running window sum to make each day O(1).

explain.intuition:
People who learned on the same day behave identically, so group them: fresh[d] is how many learn on day d. On day d, the active tellers are exactly the groups with d − forget < j ≤ d − delay: they have waited long enough but not yet forgotten. Each of them recruits one person, so fresh[d] is the sum of those groups.

At the end, the people who still remember are those who learned in the last forget days. The window of tellers slides by one day at a time, so a running sum (add the group that becomes active, drop the one that forgets) makes the whole thing linear.
steps: For each day d from 2 to n: add fresh[d − delay] to sharing if that day exists, subtract fresh[d − forget] if that day exists.
Return the sum of fresh[d] for d from n − forget + 1 to n, mod 1e9+7.
pitfalls: Letting people tell on the day they forget. On day j + forget the group is gone, as the second example shows.
Counting everyone who ever learned the rumor instead of only the last forget days of learners.
Subtracting under a modulus and ending up negative in TypeScript. Add the modulus back before taking %.

solutions.title: Sum the active window each day
solutions.idea: fresh[d] is the sum of fresh[j] over the active telling window, recomputed directly every day.

solutions.title: Running sum of active tellers
solutions.idea: Each day one group starts telling and one group forgets. Keep the number of active tellers as a running sum.

followups: n goes up to 10^18 with small delay and forget. How would a matrix power help?
Each person tells two people per day instead of one. What changes in the recurrence?
